## 1. Purpose, scope and roles

Turn observations into accountable risk decisions and discrete, testable controls. Keep treatment delivery, risk acceptance and control effectiveness separate. Opportunities can use the same decision trail but should not obscure threats.

Process identity: **P04**. Accountable process owner: **Risk process owner**.
The roles in the table perform the work. Actual appointments and deputies must be
recorded before adoption; fictional names in the example are not appointments.
This is an administrative IMS workflow, not permission to operate, isolate, repair
or restart chemical equipment.

## 2. Trigger and prerequisites

**Trigger:** A worker/customer concern, context change, incident, audit finding, proposed change or review identifies uncertainty affecting an objective.

**Required inputs/resources:** Accessible reporting channel, defined escalation contacts, scoped objective, evidence and competent participants. Management must configure risk criteria, authority limits and escalation times before operational adoption; these templates contain no universal risk matrix.

## 3. Process map and controlled steps

Capture → immediate triage → assess with affected people → leadership decision → assign controls/actions → implement → test outcome → accept/review or reopen

Use the [worksheet](ORR-FRM-RSK-001_ASSESS-RISKS-AND-DEFINE-CONTROLS-WORKSHEET.md). Each row below is a discrete proposed control:
who and when are explicit; the action/method and acceptance test are in the step;
where is the scoped process and its authorized private record store; why is the
purpose above, refined to the linked objective/risk in each execution record.
Copy each adopted control into the risk/control register with its own stable ID.

| Step | Performer | Trigger/frequency | Action and method/criteria | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Receiving supervisor | On notification | Capture the reporter’s facts, location, time, objective and potential consequence; distinguish observation from assumption. Route urgent threats through authorized emergency/stop-work arrangements. Acknowledge and name a risk owner. | Intake ID, acknowledgment, triage disposition and owner. |
| 2 | Risk owner with affected workers and relevant specialists | Before risk decision | Describe cause–event–consequence; assess existing controls and uncertainty against the organization’s recorded criteria/version. Record evidence, likelihood/consequence reasoning and assessment confidence. Do not multiply arbitrary scores to imply precision. | Assessment, criterion version, participant input and data gaps. |
| 3 | Risk owner | Before decision or leadership agenda submission | Propose treatment options and residual-risk assumptions. Write each control with performer, action, trigger, location, purpose, method/criteria and evidence; distinguish one-off actions from recurring controls. | Control statements, options, resources, action owners and due dates. |
| 4 | Authorized risk acceptor / meeting chair | At delegated decision or leadership meeting | Record accept/treat/avoid/escalate decision, reasons, resources, limits, review expiry and dissent. Only competent delegated authority may accept residual risk; unknown material consequences require investigation or escalation. | Decision ID and agenda/minutes link; acceptance boundary and conditions. |
| 5 | Action owner and control performer | By agreed due date; then at each control trigger | Implement the change and retain execution evidence. Log missed or failed executions and escalate overdue actions. A completed action does not close the parent risk. | Implementation evidence and control execution records. |
| 6 | Assurance reviewer and authorized risk acceptor | After implementation and at scheduled/change-triggered review | Test the defined outcome using the recorded method and sample. Hold outcome_pending if evidence is missing; reopen on failure and assign corrective action. Keep risk under review even after effective controls are demonstrated. | Assurance result, residual assessment, decision and next review. |

## 4. Acceptance, holds and escalation

Each material risk links an objective, an accountable decision, controls/actions and an assurance result or explicit pending state. A reviewer can test each control without guessing who acts, when, where or against what criteria.

No risk closure based only on a purchased item, revised procedure or completed training attendance. Missing authority, material uncertainty or overdue critical treatment triggers escalation. A failed control retains its parent risk and prior evidence; do not replace the risk with an unlinked new record.

Measure overdue decisions/actions, missing mandatory evidence and failed control
executions in this process; define population and review interval locally. Do not
interpret “no reports” as “no problems.” Review both performance and reporting access.

## 5. Outputs, interfaces and records

Send scope/context decisions to risk owners; risk decisions to objective/control
owners; changed methods/forms to document control; performance and unresolved
issues to management review. The receiving owner acknowledges the handoff.
Record the incoming ID, outgoing ID, sender, receiver and acceptance or rejection.
Use one authoritative operational index for completed worksheets and evidence;
retain original event identity and template revision. The public examples are not
that operational index. The worksheet defines fields and filing rules.

## 6. Configure and test before use

Replace organizational placeholders; confirm scope, actual roles, lawful obligations,
approval limits, response times, retention/access and dependencies. Have relevant
specialists verify technical criteria. Execute one normal case and one held or
failed case with intended users; record findings before approval. Use
[the shared acceptance protocol](ORR-ASP-IMP-001_BEGINNER-KIT-ACCEPTANCE.md).

## Sources, tailoring and history

Original ORR learning design, based on the user-requested ORCA chain and practical
implementation needs. A purchased commercial pack was reviewed privately for
coverage and usability lessons before drafting; this is not a clean-room claim.
No vendor procedure, diagram, spreadsheet, clause text or completed record is
included. Source provenance and limits are recorded in ORR-REG-REL-002. Existing
ORCA attribution remains in the repository SOURCES.md. These are proposed internal
methods, not verified interpretations of ISO requirements or a certification checklist.

Adopters may change layout, terminology, software and proportional detail. Keep
traceable identity, accountable decisions, applicable obligations, evidence,
failure routes and approval boundaries. Unknown is not not-applicable. A mandatory
departure requires a recorded decision within legitimate authority; internal
acceptance cannot waive external duties. Use the linked document-control procedure.
